passage:
In the hallway, the student council placed a large board called "Thank-You Board." Anyone could write a short message to thank someone at school.
The first messages were for teachers. Then students began thanking cleaners, guards, kitchen workers, and bus drivers. One message said, "Thank you to the person who always turns off the classroom lights."
No one knew who that person was, but several students smiled when they read it.
The board became full in one week. The council had to add more paper.
Before the board appeared, many people were helping the school quietly. The board did not make them work harder. It simply gave others a way to notice them.
